chapter: The Vitaphone film and studio work
title: Studio work: supplying bands and mood music on silent-film sets
summary: Spikes supplied colored bands to films and played sad or lively atmosphere music on set before sound, the only Black group doing so, earlier than Lawrence Brown.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: Did you make any other films--other than the...

Oh, I worked in a lot of films with the bands, you know, when they wanted a colored band or something. They'd call me, and I'd get whatever they wanted--a brass band or an orchestra or just a drummer--whatever they wanted, why they'd call me, and I'd get 'em. If I didn't go, I'd send somebody.
And you worked in the film studios even before sound pictures, though, right? You...you would--when they played what? Mood music, is that right? Tell me about the mood music that...

Well, uh, on the sidelines, you had...we had...had an organ and a saxophone and a...and a, uh, violin, and when they wanted sad part, well, you'd play something sad to...they called it givin' the inspiration, uh, to the...uh, puttin' them in the mood. And then you'd play lively when they needed that, and you worked on the...like that on the side. They had a lot of bands. They had several but they's the only colored one. There was only one colored.

And nobody... Hold this [the microphone] up higher. One colored band did that.

I mean one regular little orchestra like that-- three or four pieces would play, see? But they had several white bands, you know. I mean, one maybe on this set and one on that set and one on the other set.
Marshal Royal told me he played in the studios like that, I believe, and I think Lawrence Brown told me he played in the studios.
Well, they played for regular pictures.
This was a sideline thing. Lawrence told me he played in that kind of...
Atmosphere music?
Uh huh, yeah. That was the first time I think I ever heard of it was when Lawrence told me
Well, maybe they did. I don't know.
But you were probably doing it first because...

Yeah, I was doin' that afore Brown started to playin'. Brown didn't start playin', I don't think, until around '30...'29 or '28 or '29 or somethin' like that. He was...his father was a minister over in Pasadena, y'know.
Mmm hmmm, I know. So, these were jobs that people would call...that people from the studios would call the music store, and you would put together a few musicians...
Whatever they wanted.

...and go out there. And the only person... people who ever heard this music were the people working on the film 'cause it was for their...it was for the actors and actresses.

Yeah. It wasn't recorded. It was atmosphere, see? If you was gonna do a sad thing or somethin' where's people cry, you play hearts-and-flowers or something like that, you know. They... Cecil de Mille's and oldtimers William...I don't know--they would give their actors...put them in the mood.
